title: Gate receipt machine sampling crashes passing gates when proc metadata is unavailable
description:
P1-1, affected route: gate. Receipt-only machine sampling now decides whether any check can execute. tools/gate_run.py:468 reads /proc/meminfo without an error boundary; gate_one calls it at line 481 before setup/checks. A Linux sandbox which masks or denies that optional proc file still runs the original isolated gate successfully, but the reviewed head raises PermissionError, exits 1 and writes no receipt. Confirmed with the same tiny true-check fixture: main 1ddc183 exit 0/PASS; ff893f8 exit 1/PermissionError. This violates the brief's requirement that measurement cannot fail a passing gate. Preserve check/setup behavior and expose unavailable measurements explicitly with a diagnostic/error field rather than silently substituting valid-looking numbers.

Reproduction from bennett-job-gaterun, headless, TMPDIR=$PWD/.tmp/rev-gate-run-receipts-r1/tmp, CARGO_TARGET_DIR=$PWD/.tmp/rev-gate-run-receipts-r1/target. Git20/CLI30 and outer120 are existing meta fixture hang guards, not assertions:

timeout 120s python3 - <<'PY'
import subprocess, sys
from tools.tests.test_gate_run import ReceiptTests, TOOL
t = ReceiptTests()
t.setUp()
try:
    sha = t.config(checks=[["true"]])
    for rev in ("1ddc183", "ff893f8"):
        source = subprocess.check_output(
            ["git", "show", f"{rev}:tools/gate_run.py"], text=True, timeout=20)
        boot = ("import sys; sys.argv.pop(1); exec(compile(" + repr(source)
                + ", 'gate_run.py', 'exec'), {'__name__':'__main__'})")
        z = subprocess.run(
            ["bwrap", "--dev-bind", "/", "/", "--ro-bind", "/dev/null",
             "/proc/meminfo", sys.executable, "-I", "-c", boot, str(TOOL),
             "run", "--repo", str(t.repo), "--sha", sha],
            env=t.env, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30)
        print(rev, z.returncode, "PASS" if f"PASS {sha}" in z.stderr else z.stderr)
finally:
    t.doCleanups()
PY

All ordinary evidence passed: 6 receipt fixtures, 72 tools/tests, 50 gate_selftest fixtures. No real repository full gate run. Reviewed ff893f8673d1577340b24549387d286ed5f48732.
close_reason: Round 2 fix c88706a on job/gate-run-receipts, pushed wip/gate-run-receipts: independent optional receipt probes emit named unavailable exception objects, preserve check/report execution and real process statuses; accounting failures use ordinary process waiting. Red-first cases reproduced metadata crashes for meminfo/loadavg/nproc/label/wait4/CPU/RSS/width/clock and missing cache metadata. Head verification: timeout 120s python3 -m unittest discover -s tools/tests -p test_gate_run.py -v: 17 PASS in 9.706s; timeout 180s python3 -m unittest discover tools/tests: 83 PASS in 9.234s; timeout 180s python3 -I tools/gate_selftest.py: 50 PASS in 11.646s. Repeated review bwrap masked-/proc/meminfo fixture: baseline 1ddc183 and c88706a both isolated PASS/exit0; head explicitly unavailable memory. No real repository full gate. Leave bennett-zgu open per orchestrator; no further round or nit work.

title: Parallelism constants are laptop magic numbers: -j3/-j4, --test-threads=4, CARGO_BUILD_JOBS 3-4, max_workers=2 committed across repos; derive from the machine
description: Spiral (64 cores, 62 GB) 2026-11-08: every gate ran two single-threaded processes at load 2/64 because parallelism is committed at laptop values in scripts, gate.toml builds and briefs (COMMON.md 6, T3CHILD). Same antipattern as the time literals (rule 9): a per-machine fact written as a constant. Fix per repo, folded into the rule-9 sweep where it touches the same files: one machine-profile source (nproc, MemAvailable) read at run time with a per-repo cap table beside the hang-guard class table; scripts and gate.toml builds take -j and test threads from it; briefs say 'parallelism from the machine profile', never a number. Laptop behaviour unchanged (profile yields the current values there).
notes:
Maintainer 2026-11-08: 'this exposes a serious arch flaw: everything should have been exploiting multiple threads'. Verified serial loops: plugin tests/entry_snapshot.py iterates cases and entries serially (both majors run as two single-threaded isa-ref processes, 2300 s each on Spiral); arith tests/circuits/test_objects.py iterates 129 manifest entries serially (53 min; three entries of 7-14 min dominate, so a pool would cut it to ~15 min); ladder rung-1/rung-3 gate.py use ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=2); no rayon/std::thread in isa-ref, bennett-vm or the plugin. Programme, two layers: (1) HARNESS layer, fold into the rule-9 sweep per repo: every loop over independent cases (test cases, receipts, majors, repos, rung stages) runs in a pool sized from the machine profile with deterministic result ordering and per-case receipts unchanged; (2) ENGINE layer, measure first: plugin device-analysis fixpoint per-function breakdown (bp-fj1) to judge function-level parallelism; VM dense engine threads already planned (bennett-vm-bjm, do not rescope); the reference interpreter stays single-threaded by design as the trusted oracle, its harnesses parallelise around it.
Spiral s3-gate-profile 2026-11-08 (bennett/.tmp/orchestrator/s3-gate/REPORT.md + profile.json proposal): no repo has a machine profile beside a class table yet; only arith has the four-class table. Proposal: keep measured widths, keep circuit oracles serial, apply the 1.48 single-thread factor only to laptop-measured executor guards. Daily gate wall on Spiral: isa-spec 872, plugin 3094 (UNKNOWN, literal), vm 597, runtimes 472, dialect 310, sched 221, circuits 126, driver 102, estimate 50, targets 44, conformance 34; ten gates 2,828 s serial vs 872 s concurrent makespan (3.24x).

title: Meta hook passes when every discovered test is skipped
description:
scripts/pre-push:16-20 accepts a skipped-only suite: countTestCases() counts skipped cases, and unittest exits 0 for OK (skipped=1). This violates the review brief's requirement that the hook fail when no test runs; all test bodies can be deferred and the push still succeeds. Reviewed head db26f33c7e74db701d791793ffd68a7d0e43caa4. Reproduced in a scratch Git repository via the existing HookTests fixture, without altering tracked code: the assertion expecting a nonzero hook exit fails (0 == 0), with Ran 1 test / OK (skipped=1). Execute the following from bennett-job-quality-meta, headless with TMPDIR=.tmp/rev-quality-meta-r1/tmp. Run the suite once and reject zero executed, non-skipped tests; retain nonzero exit for failures/import errors and add a skipped-only regression.

timeout 30s python3 - <<'PYTEST'
import unittest
from tools.tests.test_scripts import HookTests
class NoRunnableTests(HookTests):
    def test_skipped_only_suite_is_rejected(self):
        (self.tests / 'test_fixture.py').write_text("import unittest\n@unittest.skip('deferred')\nclass Fixture(unittest.TestCase):\n    def test_fails(self): self.fail('must execute')\n")
        result = self.run_script(self.repo / 'scripts/pre-push')
        self.assertNotEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
result = unittest.TextTestRunner(verbosity=2).run(unittest.TestSuite([
    NoRunnableTests('test_skipped_only_suite_is_rejected')]))
raise SystemExit(not result.wasSuccessful())
PYTEST
close_reason: Fixed in eb3d78621cd22124f24e6571ff930c92d89b0f5f and pushed --no-verify to wip/quality-meta. The hook discovers/runs once, rejects unsuccessful results, and requires an actual successful test callback with an explicit no-tests-ran-and-passed diagnostic. Red-first: four new regressions failed on the old hook, including the review skipped-only reproduction. Verified from bennett-job-quality-meta with timeout 90s python3 -m unittest discover tools/tests: 45 tests OK (2.848s), including skipped-only, expected-failure-only, skipped-subtest-only, passing/skipped single-discovery coverage and existing pass/failure propagation. bash -n scripts/pre-push and git diff --check also exit 0.

title: Design constraint: keep the mixed fat object (native host code + device modules) reachable; no early lock-out
description:
Maintainer intent (2026-11-02): the selective-module experience is the star to follow. A brownfield program compiles with the Bennett toolchain to an ordinary native binary (x86 etc.); the user selectively marks modules/regions, and ONLY those become VM ISA objects, linked into the same binary as a fat object (north star §2 picture, §3.3 fat objects, §4.4 host-device launch ABI). It is far off ("fairly northy") and is NOT on the critical path now. What the maintainer requires today is that no early architecture decision locks it out.

Current state: every ladder rung tests whole-program device execution compared against a separately built native binary. No rung, driver mode or executor exercises a mixed binary; the host-device launch ABI is listed in the ISA spec as something it must own but is not defined; there is no classical-semantics host shim for the markers (needed to build a marker-carrying program as a plain native binary).

Standing obligation for every repo (plugin, driver, isa-spec, dialect-spec, vm, runtimes, conformance):
1. Decisions about object format, certificate layout, launch API, budgets, handle representation, effect tape and host memory by reference must state in their note or bead how a mixed fat object would use them, or name the exact change it would need. Silence is not acceptable on these topics.
2. Nothing may assume the whole program is the device program: entry points, argv/envp handling, libc closure, native comparison and certificate inventory must not hard-code "the device object is the binary".
3. Council rubric: add a check "does this contract change keep the fat object reachable?" for ISA and dialect rounds.
4. When it is cheap, prefer the choice that keeps the host/device boundary explicit (host triple IR accepted by the device lowering, handles never in host native code, markers legal as effectful external calls).

Not required now: implementing the launch ABI, the host shim, or a mixed-binary rung. File the first of those as a ladder amendment when rung 3 or 4 forces a boundary decision.
